About.title: about the band
About.subtitle: [2009 - present]
About.p1: Twenty One Pilots is an American musical band formed in 2009 in Columbus, Ohio. The band consists of drummer Josh Dun and vocalist Tyler Joseph, who is also the songwriter.
About.p2: Their music combines elements of rock, hip-hop, indie pop, reggae and alternative. The band is known for their emotional lyrics that address themes of mental health, fighting depression and inner struggles.

Tyler.name: Tyler Joseph
Tyler.descr: The ideologist of Twenty One Pilots. His lyrics are intertwined with deep meanings, and his music balances between different genres, creating the unique style of the band. Learn more about his creative path and influence on music on our website.

Josh.name: Josh Dun
Josh.descr: Drummer and energetic engine of Twenty One Pilots. His powerful drumming and stage charisma create the unique atmosphere of the band's performances. Learn more about his role and inspiration here.

Banner.title: BAND STORY
Banner.subtext: A duo from Ohio that became the voice of an entire generation. Combining indie pop, hip-hop, electronic and rock, they broke genre boundaries and built a unique musical world.

FirstMembers.title: BASEMENT CONCERTS
FirstMembers.description1: It all started in Columbus, Ohio in 2009
FirstMembers.description2: Tyler Joseph, vocalist and multi-instrumentalist, assembled the first version of the band with friends.
FirstMembers.description3: Back then, none of them knew that this band would outlive the lineup and become a global phenomenon.

FirstAlbum.p1: The debut album titled "Twenty One Pilots" was released on December 29, 2009. No labels, no producers — just faith in the idea.
FirstAlbum.p2: The album was recorded at home and distributed literally hand to hand after performances. And Joseph's mother stood at Ohio State University building and handed out tickets to their concerts.

Name.p1: The name "Twenty One Pilots" was coined by band frontman Tyler Joseph, inspired by Arthur Miller's play "All My Sons".
Name.p2: The plot centers on a businessman who sold defective parts for military aviation during World War II, leading to the death of 21 pilots.
Name.p3: This tragedy deeply affected Tyler: he saw in it the struggle between morality and personal gain — a theme that often sounds in the band's work.
Name.p4: The name Twenty One Pilots became for him a reminder of the consequences of decisions made and responsibility for them.
Name.p5: The band carried this philosophical, almost ethical message from the very beginning — and this is what distinguishes them from many other groups: they don't just sing, they ask questions.

DuoCreation.name: Josh Dun
DuoCreation.p1: Salih and Thomas left the band in 2011 to focus on work and studies. Both wrote farewell notes on the band's official Facebook page.
DuoCreation.p2: Before leaving the project, Salih invited a friend, Josh Dun (former touring drummer for House of Heroes) to take his place in the band.
DuoCreation.p3: Impressed by the band's potential and Joseph's creative vision, Dun joined the project.

SecondAlbum.p1: release of the album "Regional At Best"
SecondAlbum.p2: In 2011, the second, completely independent album was released — "Regional at Best".
SecondAlbum.p3: And although it would later be removed from distribution, it was this album that laid the foundation for the band's sound.
SecondAlbum.p4: It was then that the song "Car Radio" was born, which fans call the anthem of loneliness and inner struggle.
SecondAlbum.p5: A record label contract was already looming on the horizon. But for now it was just the story of two friends and a small scene.

Contract.t: RECORD LABEL CONTRACT AND STUDIO ALBUM
Contract.p1: signing contract with "Fueled By Ramen" label
Contract.p4: By the end of 2011, the duo could no longer be ignored. An independent band from Ohio filling venues without label help? This seemed impossible — and became a signal for the music industry.
Contract.p5: They signed a contract with Fueled By Ramen, the label that once introduced Fall Out Boy and Panic! at the Disco to the world. This became the starting point: work began on the first studio album with full producer support.
Contract.p6: Thus appeared the album "Vessel". It was released on January 8, 2013 and became a bridge between the raw emotion of the early period and the thoughtful, maniacally precise sound that made the band global. The album included updated versions of songs from Regional at Best — including "Ode to Sleep", "Guns for Hands" and "Car Radio".
Contract.p7: The Vessel cover — two old figures on a gray background. These are Tyler and Josh's grandfathers. A symbol of continuity, life, age, struggle — themes that will always run through their music.

Admire.p1: In May 2015, Blurryface was released — a concept album in which a character appears who embodies inner fears, anxieties and insecurity.
Admire.p2: He becomes a real antagonist and at the same time the voice of the album. Tyler and Josh use music as therapy — and images, stage solutions and lyrics begin to work as a unified artistic universe.
Admire.p3: But especially — "Stressed Out", which became a global hit and opened the band to millions of new listeners. With its ironic, almost childish chorus and heavy undertone of anxiety — the song perfectly reflected the spirit of the times.
Admire.p4: The Stressed Out video went viral, and the album reached #1 on the Billboard 200, turning the duo into an international sensation.

Clancy.q1: I'm the person who has to question everything, and my faith is something I've always put through heavy trials. During 'Trench' there were moments when you could see what stage of my season of doubt and re-acceptance I was in — and it was definitely a difficult time
Clancy.p1-1: Trench is not just an album. It's a story of escape from a totalitarian city controlled by nine bishops. The city is called Dema, and it became a metaphor for depression, control and emotional pain. The main character — Clancy — is trying to escape. And with him — the listener.
Clancy.p1-2: Musically, the album became more mature, cinematic, heavy. The Trench aesthetic was tied to yellow color, balaclavas, mountain jackets and visual coding.
Clancy.q2: We've always written songs for shows, not the other way around. But I've always been curious what it would be like to write an album that never existed in a concert setting.
Clancy.p2-1: The new album came out colorful, light, even almost cheerful — at first glance. The album was recorded remotely, during the pandemic. Tyler — in the basement of his house. Josh — on the other side of the country.
Clancy.p2-2: The music became lighter: synthesizers, funk rhythm, melody. But — as always with them — behind the external facade lies deep inner drama. The tracks tell about anxiety, insecurity, the attempt to seem "normal" in an abnormal world.
Clancy.q3: Much of who we are as people, and much of who we are as a band, stems from our personal insecurity about ourselves, our music, or how we present ourselves to the world.
Clancy.p3-1: The Clancy album is the culmination of the band's decade-long journey. This is not just a musical release, but the final chapter of the narrative that began in Trench and continued in Scaled and Icy. Everything converges here: images, symbols, musical ideas and internal monologues.
Clancy.p3-2: Quotes, metaphors, references to past albums — everything is woven into the poetics that fans love to decipher.
Clancy.p3-3: Clancy sounds like a synthesis of raw, live drums, deep bass, alternative rock, rap, and even industrial.
Clancy.p3-4: This is an album not about victory, but about the ability not to give up. This is the sound of a person who has learned to look fear in the face — and not look away. This is the end of the story. And the beginning of yourself.
